subject.title: [Bug]: reclaim of a cloud session with a retained keep-local conflict fails on quiescence, then wedges on "has active work"

question: Should the cloud-worker owner treat this as the remaining reclaim-stop failure mode and prioritize a focused current-main reproduction plus repair, rather than broadening the existing release condition without validating the staged-result fence invariants?
rationale: The necessary change sits at the boundary between quiescence safety, durable staged-result recovery, and work-claim release; choosing the wrong release condition can reintroduce result loss.

options.title: Reproduce and patch the bounded failure path
options.body: Confirm the keep-local staged-ref scenario on the current head, then add a narrow fix and regression coverage for both retryability and durable-result preservation.

options.title: Request a refreshed trace first
options.body: Keep the issue assigned while obtaining a current-head trace if the existing scenario no longer reaches the reported quiescence failure.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and patch the bounded failure path
recommendation.body: Confirm the keep-local staged-ref scenario on the current head, then add a narrow fix and regression coverage for both retryability and durable-result preservation.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior merged reclaim and durable-result work makes this contributor the strongest history-based routing candidate for the failure boundary.
